name: Claudia Sheinbaum
role: President of Mexico — Quintuple Bilateral Pressure Track: CIA Chihuahua + DOJ Rocha Moya + Extradition Standard + State Dept Consulate Review + CJNG Framework, May 2026
quote: There are no joint operations on land or in the air. [April 24: Formal letter to all 32 governors — foreign security cooperation through federal channels only.] [April 28: Maru Campos declined Senate hearing — 'The investigation must continue.'] [April 30: DOJ SDNY indicts Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya.] [May 2: Rocha Moya 'temporary leave' — first sitting Mexican governor to step down under U.S. drug charges.] [May 6: EXTRADITION INFLECTION — Mexico requires 'overwhelming and irrefutable proof' before extraditing U.S.-indicted officials.] [May 7–8: U.S. STATE DEPT began formal review of all 53 Mexican consulates in the U.S.] [May 7: Trump warns 'if they're not gonna do the job, we will' — Sheinbaum responds: 'This isn't the first time he has made such statements, but we are taking action,' citing 50% homicide decline and 2,500 labs destroyed.] [May 9: El Chucky (CJNG Manzanillo plaza boss) arrested — counter-CJNG enforcement continues in parallel with bilateral tensions.] [May 11–12: Plan Kukulkan enters 30-day final phase — 111,000+ security personnel mobilized for FIFA World Cup 2026 (opening June 11, Mexico City); Guadalajara (4 matches) under heightened CJNG-specific security framework.] [May 12: ACLED assessment published — CJNG shows zero organizational fracture 79 days post-Mencho; CJNG reinforcing Michoacán alliances with Los Viagras.] [May 12–13: CNN EXCLUSIVE — CIA Ground Branch operatives participated in lethal anti-cartel operations inside Mexico, including a March 2026 highway killing of Francisco Beltran ('El Payin'). García Harfuch formal denial: 'There are no foreign operations on Mexican soil.' CIA denies report.] [May 14: FGR CIAgate criminal investigation confirmed — FGR adds jurisdictional invasion line to national security crimes file; possible 'treason against nation' charges; Chihuahua Strategic Operations Fiscal resigned.] [May 15: Mexican federal tribunal ratified El Jardinero extradition suspension — FGR's amparo declared inadmissible; El Jardinero faces Mexican justice first. DOJ superseding indictment issued (meth trafficking + money laundering + weapons). El Cabo vinculado a proceso for Teuchitlán/La Galera forced recruitment.] [May 16–17: GUERRERO DISPLACEMENT CRISIS — Washington Post documented Los Ardillos drone bomb attacks on indigenous Guerrero communities; 800+ displaced, 3 community police killed. CJNG CHILE TRIAL (May 17): Chilean prosecutors seeking 35-year sentences for CJNG nationals who produced 844kg meth in Chile — documents cartel transnational resilience.] [May 17–19 — DAY 86: LAGOS DE MORENO NARCOCREMATORIO — Madres Buscadoras discover active CJNG crematory and training center still burning; 16+ fosas, 60 bags of human remains at El Salto; linked to El Cabo (arrested May 7). 23 days to FIFA World Cup. Quintuple bilateral pressure track at maximum stress.] [May 20–21 — DAYS 87–88: CJNG AFRICA LABS — U.S. AFRICOM warned Congress that CJNG and Sinaloa have established meth labs in Africa (South Africa primary; 12 labs identified, 11 intercepted; 4 Mexican nationals detained near Swarttruggens). La Jornada confirmed May 21. Together with Chile meth hub, documents CJNG transnational manufacturing arc on two continents.] [May 22 — DAY 89: CJNG NAHUA COMMUNITY ATTACKS — La Jornada: three CJNG armed attacks against La Cofradía and Ostula (Aquila, Michoacán) in three days (May 19–21); 42 homicides + 5 disappearances documented in 18 months; urgent demand for federal military deployment. NIGERIA METH BUST: NDLEA raids CJNG-linked superlab in Ogun State — 2,419 kg meth, 3 Mexican nationals arrested ($362.9M); adds West Africa node to the CJNG transnational arc.] [May 21–22 — DAY 90: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN VISIT — Sheinbaum and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin met at the National Palace on May 21–22, pledging bilateral security cooperation 'rooted in mutual respect.' Sheinbaum: 'The security relationship is one of collaboration and coordination, not subordination.' Next high-level bilateral security meeting scheduled for June 2026. Mullin acknowledged Mexico's security efforts without new operational demands. CIA tensions addressed within September 2025 bilateral framework. 'Coordination without subordination' established as governing principle for Plan Kukulkan World Cup security sprint.] [May 24 — DAY 91: INTERNATIONAL MEDIA SPOTLIGHT — KVIA (May 21): 1,907 bodies found in Guadalajara metro since 2018; 226 sets of remains in 58 graves since Jan 2025; 45,000 minors recruited by CJNG. The Week (May 24): 'How Mexico's cartel wars cast a shadow over the FIFA World Cup' — CJNG in 40+ countries, franchise model resilient to 91 days of decapitation. U.S. special forces confirmed training Mexican military on stadium attack prevention and drone bomb defense.] [May 25 — DAY 92: DOJ CHINESE NATIONALS INDICTMENT — U.S. DOJ charged Ruhuan Zhen and Hongce Wu for laundering drug proceeds for both CJNG and the Sinaloa Cartel via transnational Chinese underground banking networks. The dual-cartel scope confirms Chinese financial intermediaries operate across cartel lines. EL SAPO HUNT (Day 92): No capture. PLAN KUKULKAN: 17 days to FIFA World Cup opening. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID Day 16. CIAGATE FGR INVESTIGATION: Ongoing.] [May 28 — DAY 95: CJNG KENYA METH LAB — First East Africa CJNG presence confirmed (Kenyan government + U.S. AFRICOM 2026 Posture Statement); extends transnational manufacturing arc to four continents. PLAN KUKULKAN: 14 days to FIFA World Cup opening (June 11). EL SAPO HUNT: At large, Day 95. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID: Day 19. CIAGATE FGR INVESTIGATION: Ongoing. June bilateral Mullin meeting scheduled. DOJ TERRORISM PRECEDENT (May 16): First-ever CJNG operative charged under 'material support of terrorism' statutes.] [May 29 — DAY 96: CJNG COLOMBIAN MERCENARIES PURÉPECHA — Michoacán AG formally confirmed 60+ Colombian paramilitary operatives embedded with CJNG in 10 Purépecha Plateau municipalities. PLAN KUKULKAN: 13 days.] [May 30 — DAY 97: CARTEL FIFA BLACKOUT DIRECTIVE — CJNG and Jalisco cartel factions reportedly issued internal orders to avoid high-visibility violence during the World Cup tournament; analysts assess as temporary operational calculus, not structural change. PLAN KUKULKAN: 12 days. EL SAPO HUNT: At large, Day 97.] [May 31 — DAY 98: CNN WORLD CUP SECURITY ASSESSMENT — CNN published May 31 security assessment flagging CJNG shadow over Guadalajara's 4 World Cup matches. PLAN KUKULKAN: 11 days to FIFA opening. June bilateral Mullin meeting scheduled for post-World Cup reset. EL SAPO HUNT: At large, Day 98. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID: Day 22.] [June 2 — DAY 100 MILESTONE: 8 nations — US, Canada, UK, Australia, Germany, France, New Zealand, Japan — issued heightened Mexico travel warnings ahead of the FIFA World Cup. PLAN KUKULKAN T-9.] [June 3 — DAY 101: U.S. DOJ announced CJNG-linked NC drug cell leader Elian Rene Fabian Valladolid sentenced to 262 months. World Cup trilateral US-Mexico-Canada security framework reported (Sunday Independent).] [June 4 — DAY 102: HSToday documented CJNG-authorized bounties on U.S. CBP agents via drone/gunfire — cross-border threat escalation.] [June 5 — DAY 103: MEXICO-FIFA FINAL SECURITY REVIEW — Mexican security authorities met FIFA officials (ESPN) for final pre-tournament assessment. PLAN KUKULKAN T-6. OCCRP INVESTIGATION: 'Fear Is the Message' — CJNG weaponized social media algorithms to paralyze Mexican society. EL SAPO AT LARGE — DAY 103.] [June 6 — DAY 104: KOREA DAY IN ZAPOPAN — South Korea's World Cup squad held cultural event in CJNG's historic operational heartland (Zapopan, Guadalajara metro); InSight Crime assessed cartel groups unlikely to target tourists, but Jalisco has ~16,000 disappearances. PLAN KUKULKAN T-5. CJNG BLACKOUT DIRECTIVE confirmed ongoing.] [June 7 — DAY 105: PLAN KUKULKAN T-4 DAYS — fully operational at all three World Cup venues. GUADALAJARA VIOLENCE -30% pre-tournament (Rio Times, Open The Magazine). EL SAPO AT LARGE — DAY 105: Pre-June 11 capture objective definitively unmet; World Cup perimeter security is Mexico's primary security posture. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID: Day 29. JUNE BILATERAL MULLIN MEETING: Not yet formally calendared.] (Sources: CBC News, CBS News, Latin Times, Al Jazeera, CNN, PBS, Borderland Beat, Chatham House, ACLED/Proceso, La Jornada, Milenio, La Silla Rota, Washington Times, DOJ, Washington Post, El Mostrador, Infobae, Proceso, Publimetro, El Financiero, Diario de Yucatán, Arise News, NDLEA, KVIA/Puente News Collaborative, The Week, Mexico News Daily, Sky Sports, Townhall, Citizen Digital Kenya, AFRICOM, Mexicanist, Total News Agency, CSIS, ESPN, Sunday Independent, SBA/DOJ, OCCRP, Nomad Lawyer, Seoul Economic Daily, Rio Times Online, Open The Magazine — April 24 – June 7, 2026)

name: María Eugenia Campos Galván
role: Chihuahua Governor ('Maru Campos') — PAN — DECLINED Senate CIA Hearing April 28, 2026
quote: Maru Campos declined to appear at the April 28, 2026 Senate hearing on CIA agents in Chihuahua — sending an official letter citing need to protect ongoing investigations. Direct statement: 'No, we are not going to attend the Senate today because it is not mandatory. We answer to our people, not to the Senate.' Senate Political Coordination Board president Ignacio Mier condemned her no-show as an 'institutional crisis in Chihuahua.' Sheinbaum response: 'The investigation must continue.' The CIA sovereignty governance crisis remains unresolved: Sheinbaum's April 24-25 governance reform letter to 32 governors stands as executive policy, but the failed Senate hearing leaves the constitutional question of state-level bilateral security cooperation unanswered. (Sources: La Silla Rota, Proceso, El Financiero — April 28, 2026)

name: Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes
role: CJNG Founder & Supreme Leader (d. Feb 22, 2026)
quote: El Mencho built the most powerful criminal organization in the Western Hemisphere from a rural Michoacán village. His February 2026 death leaves a power vacuum with no clear successor.

name: Juan Carlos Valencia González
role: CJNG New Leader — Confirmed by El País (Apr 6, 2026) ('O3') — $5M U.S. Bounty
quote: El País (April 6, 2026) confirmed O3 as CJNG's new leader — the most credible international media confirmation of the post-Mencho succession to date. As El Mencho's stepson and commander of Grupo Élite, CJNG's paramilitary unit, O3 commands the cartel's greatest concentrated firepower. Born September 12, 1984 in Santa Ana, California — his U.S. citizenship creates unique legal exposure and complicates bilateral targeting options. Succession field has narrowed significantly: El Doble R arrested, El Tuli killed, El Jardinero primary remaining rival. (Sources: El País, InSight Crime, U.S. State Dept, IBTimes UK)

name: Ricardo Ruiz Velasco
role: CJNG Senior Operational Commander ('El Doble R') — ARRESTED March 11, 2026
quote: Arrested March 11, 2026 in Mexicali, Baja California — charged with homicide, terrorist acts, and armed robbery. El Doble R was widely considered the top succession candidate after El Mencho. His capture eliminates the most formidable internal consolidator from the succession race, narrowing the field to O3 and El Jardinero. (Sources: La Silla Rota, El Financiero)

name: Audias Flores Silva
role: CJNG Senior Regional Commander ('El Jardinero') — ARRESTED APRIL 27, 2026 — Fractura Total Faction Leader Captured
quote: ARRESTED April 27 + DOJ SUPERSEDING INDICTMENT May 14 + EXTRADITION SUSPENDED May 15: Audias Flores Silva 'El Jardinero' was captured April 27, 2026, near El Mirador, Nayarit — found hiding in a roadside drainage ditch ~20km north of Puerto Vallarta after a 19-month surveillance operation involving 500+ troops, 6 helicopters, and multiple aircraft. No shots fired; César Alejandro 'El Güero Conta' (his financial operator) simultaneously arrested in Zapopan. El Jardinero served as El Mencho's longtime security chief and declared war on O3/Los Cuinis on April 11, 2026 (Fractura Total) — deploying Monstruos armored vehicles along the Jalisco-Zacatecas border (April 18) and attacking a police HQ (April 12). His capture effectively ends Fractura Total as an organized armed opposition to O3. [May 4: Vinculado a proceso at Altiplano.] [May 14: U.S. DOJ federal grand jury in Washington D.C. issued superseding indictment — expanding existing 2020 charges (cocaine/heroin) to include meth trafficking, money laundering conspiracy, and use of a destructive device; faces minimum 10 years to life if convicted.] [May 15: Mexican federal tribunal ratified the suspension blocking his U.S. extradition — FGR's amparo declared inadmissible. He will face Mexican criminal proceedings first; extradition timeline indeterminate.] El Sapo remains the sole senior anti-O3 faction leader at large. (Sources: CBS News, Al Jazeera, La Silla Rota, Latin Times — April 27–28; DOJ press release, Washington Times, Infobae, SDP Noticias — May 14–15, 2026)

name: Rosalinda González Valencia
role: El Mencho's Wife — CJNG Financial Operations ('La Jefa')
quote: Released early from a five-year money laundering sentence in early 2025 for 'good conduct,' sparking controversy. Rosalinda's González Valencia family connections to Los Cuinis made her CJNG's key financial architect. She remains free and under scrutiny.

name: Omar García Harfuch
role: Mexico Security Secretary — Led Post-Mencho Operation
quote: The man CJNG tried to kill in June 2020 ended up overseeing the operation that killed El Mencho in February 2026. As Security Secretary and former intelligence director, García Harfuch personifies Mexico's decade-long escalation against CJNG.

name: General Ricardo Trevilla Trejo
role: SEDENA Secretary (Mexican Defense Minister)
quote: Led the institutional military planning behind the Tapalpa operation. SEDENA under Trevilla has deepened intelligence-sharing with U.S. NORTHCOM and DEA while maintaining operational command authority over cartel interdiction missions on Mexican soil.

name: Claudia Sheinbaum
role: President of Mexico (since Oct 2024)
quote: Sheinbaum inherited Mexico's cartel crisis from AMLO and has navigated between maintaining her predecessor's social-investment approach and cooperating more closely with U.S. security demands following CJNG's FTO designation and the February 2026 El Mencho operation.

name: DEA Administrator
role: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration — Lead CJNG Targeting Agency
quote: DEA has designated CJNG as one of the highest-priority Consolidated Priority Organization Targets (CPOTs). Operation Python (2020) and the sustained intelligence campaign against El Mencho represent the DEA's most intensive sustained targeting effort against a single cartel.

name: Marco Rubio
role: U.S. Secretary of State — Signed CJNG FTO Designation
quote: Secretary Rubio officially designated CJNG as a Foreign Terrorist Organization on February 20, 2025, implementing the Trump executive order and marking a major escalation in U.S. legal treatment of Mexican cartels. The designation enabled new prosecution tools against material supporters.

name: Rubén Oseguera González
role: CJNG Former Second-in-Command (Imprisoned, U.S.) — 'El Menchito'
quote: El Mencho's son and former heir apparent was extradited to the U.S. in 2020 and sentenced to life plus 30 years in March 2025, with a $6 billion forfeiture order. His imprisonment sealed CJNG's succession crisis before his father's death.

name: Érick Valencia Salazar
role: CJNG Co-founder ('El 85') — PLEADED GUILTY April 7, 2026 in U.S. Federal Court
quote: One of CJNG's original four co-founders, El 85 pleaded guilty on April 7, 2026 in U.S. District Court in Washington D.C. to conspiracy to distribute cocaine for importation into the United States — facing life in prison. Sentencing: July 31, 2026. Arrested by Mexican Army in Zapopan, Jalisco in March 2012 (triggering 12 narcobloqueos); he later broke from El Mencho to found La Nueva Plaza, a rival cartel. Extradited to U.S. February 27, 2025, part of the historic 29-figure mass extradition. His guilty plea closes the prosecution chapter on three of CJNG's four original co-founders: El Mencho (killed Feb 22, 2026), El 53 (killed 2019 by CJNG hitman), El 85 (now in U.S. custody). (Sources: U.S. DOJ, Washington Post, Washington Times)

name: José Antonio Yépez Ortiz
role: Former Santa Rosa de Lima Cartel Leader — CJNG's Rival ('El Marro')
quote: CSRL leader whose August 2020 arrest handed CJNG a decisive advantage in Guanajuato. El Marro became a social-media-savvy cartel boss who posted videos defending his gang's role in defending communities from CJNG, but ultimately could not sustain military resistance without state protection.

name: Los Viagras Leadership
role: Michoacán Rival Cartel — CJNG's Persistent Enemy in Tierra Caliente
quote: Originally a community self-defense group, Los Viagras evolved into a criminal enterprise competing with CJNG over Michoacán's avocado and lime extortion rackets. Their knowledge of local terrain gives them a 'profound advantage' in Tierra Caliente despite CJNG's superior firepower.

name: Mexican Human Rights Defenders
role: Civil Society — Documenting Cartel and State Violence
quote: Journalists and rights defenders documenting CJNG violence face severe retaliation. Mexico has remained one of the world's most dangerous countries for journalists for over a decade, with CJNG-linked threats and killings documented across Jalisco, Colima, Michoacán, and Veracruz.

name: Heraclio Guerrero Martínez
role: CJNG Regional Commander for Michoacán/Jalisco ('Tío Lako') — Head of 'Los Guerrero' Cell, Still At Large as Hunt Continues
quote: Longtime CJNG regional operator rooted in Tinaja de Vargas, Tanhuato, Michoacán, and head of the family-based 'Los Guerrero' cell; brother of 'Los Guerreros' founder Javier Guerrero Martínez, godfather to El Mencho. Authorities allege he ordered attacks on National Guard personnel following the February 22 Tapalpa operation; his son died in that same operation. On August 19, 2026, federal forces raided cells tied to him in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, Michoacán, detaining 9 people including his daughter Marisol 'N' and romantic partner Lourdes 'N,' and seizing heavy weapons, grenade launchers, IEDs, and a drone; 3 additional detentions brought the total tied to the operation to 12. CJNG retaliated with roadblocks and vehicle burnings across roughly a dozen Michoacán municipalities. STILL AT LARGE (Aug 22): La Jornada reported the hunt for Guerrero Martínez continuing across Michoacán and Jalisco, with federal sources unable to confirm his capture, death, or escape — his name does not appear on official detention lists. No U.S. reward has been confirmed for him specifically as of August 24, 2026.

name: Julio Alberto Castillo Rodríguez
role: CJNG Lieutenant ('El Chorro') — Named El Mencho's Son-in-Law, Reports to El 03 ($15M U.S. Bounty)
quote: Previously known only as one of eight leaders named in the DOJ/State Department's $102M coordinated reward package (August 5, 2026), which set a $15M bounty on him alongside El Sapo and El Jardinero. In an August 22, 2026 six-month retrospective on CJNG's post-Mencho reorganization, Infobae identified Castillo Rodríguez as El Mencho's son-in-law and a lieutenant reporting directly to Juan Carlos Valencia González ('El 03'), positioning him within the cartel's reorganized inner circle alongside military-wing counterpart Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán ('El Sapo'). Status as of August 24, 2026: at large. (Sources: DOJ/State Department reward announcement, Aug 5; Infobae, Aug 22, 2026)

name: InSight Crime / Crisis Group Analysts
role: Independent Organized Crime Research Organizations
quote: InSight Crime and the International Crisis Group have provided the most sustained independent analysis of CJNG's structure, tactics, and succession dynamics. Their assessments consistently warn that decapitation strategies risk fragmentation that produces more violence, not less.

name: Hugo César Macías Ureña
role: CJNG Chief Financial/Logistics Officer ('El Tuli') — KILLED Feb 22, 2026
quote: Killed by Mexican special forces in El Grullo, Jalisco, in a parallel operation on Feb 22 — the same day as El Mencho. El Tuli served as CJNG's top financial/logistics architect. He had offered 20,000-peso bounties per soldier killed in retaliation. $965,000 USD and 7.2M pesos seized at time of death.

name: Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán
role: CJNG Military Chief & Top Priority Target ('El Sapo' / 'El 090') — NAMED TOP-2 FEDERAL SECURITY CABINET TARGET (May 3, 2026)
quote: FEDERAL SECURITY CABINET TOP-2 TARGET (May 3, 2026): Mexico's Federal Security Cabinet identified El Sapo as one of the two top-priority CJNG targets alongside El 03. As CJNG's military chief, El Sapo controls sicario recruitment and training centers — including Rancho Izaguirre in Teuchitlán, Jalisco — and manages territorial operations across Jalisco, Michoacán, and Puebla. His personal security detail includes former Mexican Army, Marines, and Colombian and Guatemalan former combatants. Controls drug trafficking logistics through Zacatecas and Baja California corridors and coordinates Chinese fentanyl precursor acquisition networks through the Puerto Vallarta-Manzanillo corridor. With El Jardinero arrested April 27, El Sapo is now the last surviving organized military faction leadership figure, positioning him as El 03's most significant internal CJNG counterpart rather than an external threat. The El 03 vs. El Sapo succession dynamic — finance wing vs. military wing — mirrors historical post-decapitation cartel splits that have previously resolved violently. PUERTO VALLARTA PLAZA BOSS CONFIRMED (Jul 23, 2026): OFAC's largest-ever CJNG sanctions action formally designated him as CJNG's plaza boss for Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco. $15M U.S. REWARD (Aug 5, 2026): Named among the 8 CJNG leaders in the $102M coordinated DOJ/State reward package. Status as of Day 169 (Aug 10, 2026): at large; active CJNG military commander and Puerto Vallarta plaza boss; top federal targeting priority. (Sources: La Jornada, El Imparcial, La Jornada San Luis, U.S. Treasury OFAC, Borderland Beat — May 3–Aug 5, 2026)

name: Juan Carlos Valencia González ('O3')
role: CJNG New Leader — Confirmed Apr 6, 2026 (El País) — Grupo Élite Commander
quote: El País confirmed O3 as CJNG's new leader on April 6, 2026 — the most authoritative international media confirmation of the succession. Previously reported per anonymous cartel source (March 2026) and consistent with U.S. NCTC's pre-Mencho assessment of O3 as 'de facto second-in-command.' Born in Santa Ana, California (September 12, 1984), O3 is a U.S. citizen — creating legal complications for bilateral targeting operations. As Grupo Élite commander, he controls CJNG's greatest concentrated paramilitary firepower. Succession field has narrowed: El Doble R arrested (March 11, later corrected — see below), El Tuli killed (February 22). El Jardinero's regional power in Jalisco, Nayarit, Zacatecas, Michoacán remains a rival center. OFAC LARGEST-EVER CJNG ACTION (Jul 23, 2026): U.S. Treasury formally sanctioned him and 50+ other CJNG individuals/entities, confirming him as cartel leader. REWARD RAISED TO $25M (Aug 5, 2026): U.S. State Dept/DOJ raised his bounty from $5M to $25M — matching historic Maduro- and bin Laden-tier reward levels — as part of a coordinated $102M package targeting 8 CJNG leaders. SIX-MONTH RETROSPECTIVE (Aug 22, 2026): Infobae assessed El 03 as having assumed absolute control of an organization now estimated at 15,000-20,000 members operating across 8 states (Jalisco, Nayarit, Colima, Veracruz, Guanajuato, Puebla, Querétaro, Hidalgo) under a hybrid hierarchical/franchise model, with lieutenants 'El Chorro' (Julio Alberto Castillo Rodríguez, son-in-law) and 'El Sapo' beneath him; DEA's Terry Cole reiterated he remains the agency's 'priority number one.' [Sources: El País, InSight Crime, IBTimes UK, U.S. State Department, U.S. Treasury OFAC, Washington Examiner, Infobae — April–August 2026]

name: Omar García Harfuch
role: Mexico Security Secretary — El Pepe Arrest Statement, Mar 16
quote: The arrest of 'El Pepe' in Tlajomulco de Zúñiga represents the closure of a critical intelligence gap. This individual transported El Mencho's companion to the Tapalpa hideout — the link in the chain that ultimately led to the elimination of the most wanted criminal in Mexico's history. Mexico's security forces are systematically dismantling the entire network that protected El Mencho for decades.

name: Omar García Harfuch
role: Mexico Security Secretary — CJNG Threat Assessment, Mar 21, 2026
quote: El CJNG es una organización criminal que opera en todo el país. Despite the historic elimination of El Mencho and the sustained post-Tapalpa pressure campaign, the cartel's national operational footprint remains intact. Mexico's security forces will continue systematic dismantlement of CJNG's network — but citizens and businesses across all 27 affected states should remain vigilant.

name: Fernando Daniel Farías de la Cruz
role: CJNG Forced-Recruiter for Rancho Izaguirre / Teuchitlán ('El Cabo') — ARRESTED May 7, 2026, Ciudad Acuña, Coahuila
quote: ARRESTED: Fernando Daniel Farías de la Cruz 'El Cabo' was captured May 7, 2026 at a property in Ciudad Acuña, Coahuila — approximately 1,100 km from his operational base at the Rancho Izaguirre / 'La Galera' compound in Teuchitlán, Jalisco. The AIC (Agencia de Investigación Criminal) arrested him on charges of crimes against health, enforced disappearances (desaparición forzada), and organized crime/human trafficking. He was transferred to CEFERESO Puente Grande, Jalisco. As the CJNG's forced-recruitment operator for Teuchitlán — the extermination compound where FGR found nearly 100 DNA samples and bone fragments predating 2015 — his arrest extends the FGR's methodical dismantlement of El Sapo's military infrastructure chain: El Jardinero (arrested Apr 27) → El Güero Conta (arrested Apr 27) → El Cabo (arrested May 7). (Sources: Aristegui Noticias, El Financiero, Infobae México — May 7–8, 2026)

name: Lorenzo Sánchez
role: CJNG Manzanillo Plaza Boss ('El Chucky') — ARRESTED May 9, 2026, Bahía de Santiago
quote: ARRESTED: Lorenzo Sánchez 'El Chucky' was captured May 9, 2026 in the exclusive Bahía de Santiago residential area of Manzanillo, Colima, by federal and state forces using aerial drone surveillance and coordinated ground operations. No shots were fired. Charges: homicide, kidnapping, extortion, and narcotics distribution. As CJNG's plaza boss for Manzanillo — Mexico's busiest Pacific port and the primary entry point for Chinese fentanyl precursors — El Chucky's removal represents the most strategically significant port-sector arrest of the post-Mencho decapitation campaign. His arrest follows the April 16 arrest of eight Manzanillo police for leaking C5i intelligence to CJNG via Threema, constituting a two-phase dismantlement of CJNG's Manzanillo sector: intelligence corruption network (April 16) → plaza boss (May 9). Analysts assess a successor plaza boss will be designated by El 03's Grupo Élite within 1–2 weeks. (Sources: Borderland Beat, Parriva, La Jornada San Luis — May 9, 2026)

name: FGR (Fiscalía General de la República)
role: Mexican Attorney General — El Mencho Evidence Handling Statement, Mar 2026
quote: No había condiciones para resguardar los inmuebles donde hallaron la narconómina de 'El Mencho.' The properties where El Mencho's financial ledgers and payroll records were discovered could not be adequately secured immediately after the February 22 operation. The FGR is working to preserve the evidentiary value of all materials found. Critics and opposition lawmakers have demanded a formal investigation into potential evidence tampering at the sites.

name: Ronald Johnson
role: U.S. Ambassador to Mexico — Warning to CJNG Leader 'El 03,' Aug 8, 2026; 'International Reach Is Vulnerability' Statement, Aug 12
quote: Ya no hay dónde esconderse. Los encontraremos y rendirán cuentas. (There is nowhere left to hide. We will find them and they will be held accountable.) — Posted on X directly addressing Juan Carlos Valencia González ('El 03'), days after the State Department raised its bounty on him to $25 million as part of the August 5 reward package targeting eight CJNG leaders. [Aug 12: Following the DOJ's unsealing of Czech Republic weapons-trafficking charges against four CJNG members, Johnson told Mexican press: 'El alcance internacional del CJNG también es su vulnerabilidad. Estos cargos envían un mensaje claro al CJNG y a otras organizaciones narcoterroristas: dondequiera que operen, los perseguiremos.' (CJNG's international reach is also its vulnerability. These charges send a clear message: wherever they operate, we will pursue them.)]

name: Unnamed CJNG Special-Operations Member
role: CJNG Operative — On-Camera Leadership Confirmation, ARTEde Documentary, Aug 7, 2026
quote: El Mencho siempre será nuestro líder, pero ahora nuestro comandante es el 03. Es la autoridad y el poder... Quien desafíe su poder será castigado. El cártel está por encima de todo. Es una maquinaria enorme. (El Mencho will always be our leader, but now our commander is El 03. He is the authority and the power... Whoever defies his power will be punished. The cartel is above everything. It's an enormous machine.) — First on-the-record acknowledgment from within CJNG's own ranks of El 03's succession, in the German documentary 'Los cárteles mexicanos: ¿El fin de la impunidad?'

name: Gregory W. Kehoe
role: U.S. Attorney, Middle District of Florida — Czech Republic CJNG Charges, Aug 11, 2026
quote: ANNOUNCED CHARGES: Kehoe unsealed narcoterrorism, material-support-to-terrorism, drug-importation, and arms-trafficking charges against four CJNG members — Edgar Alejandro López Velasco, Noé Díaz Jiménez, José Miguel Alvarado Morales, and Leobardo Gaxiola López ('Bado') — arrested in the Czech Republic in June 2026. Prosecutors allege the group brokered European military-grade weapons (machine guns, rocket launchers, mortars, explosives) in exchange for fentanyl and methamphetamine shipments destined for U.S. distribution. Two defendants were extradited to Florida; two remain detained in Europe pending extradition. All face potential life sentences if convicted.

name: Terry Cole
role: DEA Administrator — 'Global Hunt' Announcement Against CJNG, Aug 13, 2026
quote: CJNG, a designated foreign terrorist organization, is killing a record number of Americans. They are a terrorist organization and will be treated as such. La DEA nunca ha estado tan enfocada como hoy en combatir al CJNG y a sus líderes. (The DEA has never been as focused as it is today on fighting CJNG and its leaders.) — Announced at a Tampa, Florida press conference alongside the DOJ's Czech Republic narcoterrorism case, pledging a coordinated global law-enforcement campaign (DEA, ATF, FBI, DHS, Coast Guard) across offices in Mexico City, Vienna, Cartagena, Portugal, Tampa, and New York, backed by the $102M reward package. Closed with a direct warning to the cartel: 'vamos por ustedes' (we're coming for you).

name: Iván Cazarín Molina ('El Tanque')
role: CJNG Founding-Generation Figure / Veracruz Fuel-Theft (Huachicol) Operator
quote: NAMED IN LORET DE MOLA AUDIO (Aug 18, 2026): 2023 recordings released by Carlos Loret de Mola quote Luis Alberto Olán — brother of Andy López Beltrán associate Jorge Amílcar Olán Aparicio — citing his relationship with Cazarín Molina to explain halting extortion of a gravel-mine supplier tied to López Beltrán's network ('yo conozco a El Tanque'). Cazarín Molina, alias 'El Tanque,' is a CJNG founding-generation associate of El Mencho who built a multimillion-liter illegal fuel-storage and distribution network in Veracruz (branded gas stations including 'Etanofuel' and 'G Energy') by tapping Pemex pipelines. The U.S. Treasury's OFAC sanctioned him in September 2024 alongside his brother César 'Tornado' Cazarín Molina and other network members for CJNG-linked fuel theft.

name: Andrés 'Andy' López Beltrán
role: Morena National Secretary of Organization / Son of Former President López Obrador
quote: IMPLICATED IN LORET DE MOLA AUDIO (Aug 18, 2026): Carlos Loret de Mola released 2023 recordings of close friend and financial operator Jorge Amílcar Olán Aparicio and his brother Luis Alberto discussing coordination with a CJNG fuel-theft and extortion cell in Veracruz via operator Iván Cazarín Molina ('El Tanque'). López Beltrán had not issued a specific response to this release as of the update. Responding to Loret's earlier May 2026 allegations that he and brother Gonzalo 'Bobby' received narco-linked payments, López Beltrán wrote on Instagram: 'De no presentar dichas pruebas seguiremos asumiendo lo que siempre hemos sabido. Eres un periodista mercenario' ('If you don't present such proof, we'll keep assuming what we've always known. You're a mercenary journalist'), calling the reporting 'calumnias' serving 'intereses mezquinos.'

name: Francisco Álvarez Solorio
role: Son of CJNG 'Los Rs' Cell Leader 'El R-1' / Accused in Valeria Márquez Femicide
quote: BREAKS SILENCE FROM HIDING (Aug 21, 2026): In an interview with journalist Luis Chaparro, Álvarez Solorio — accused by Security Secretary García Harfuch of threatening influencer Valeria Márquez and asking his father 'El R-1' to order her May 13, 2025 killing — said: 'Mira, honestamente, me siento un poco atemorizado y atacado hacia mi persona.' He denied ordering or knowing who ordered Márquez's death and said the two had discussed reconciling. He remains a fugitive; his father was arrested July 30, 2026 in Atotonilco el Alto, Jalisco.

name: C.M.M.M. ('El Abulón')
role: Second-in-Command, 'Los Mezcales' (CJNG-Linked Armed Wing, Colima)
quote: CAPTURED IN OAXACA (Aug 21, 2026): Identified by SEMAR and the Oaxaca state prosecutor's office as second-in-command of 'Los Mezcales,' also known by aliases 'El Coco,' 'El Pena,' 'La Iguana,' and 'León.' Blamed by authorities as one of the main generators of violence in Colima state — homicides, extortion, and territorial disputes across Colima, Villa de Álvarez, Tecomán, Armería, and the port city of Manzanillo. Captured in a private residential development in Ejido Guadalupe Victoria, north of Oaxaca de Juárez.

name: Rafael Álvarez Ayala ('El R-2')
role: Successor Leader, CJNG-Affiliated 'Los Rs' Cell (Michoacán/Jalisco) — Charged, At Large
quote: NAMED SUCCESSOR TO 'EL R-1' (Aug 27, 2026): Brother of Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala ('El R-1,' arrested Jul 30, 2026 in Atotonilco el Alto, Jalisco). Mexican authorities identify El R-2 as having assumed leadership of 'Los Rs,' a CJNG-affiliated cell operating across Apatzingán, Uruapan, and Morelia, Michoacán. A Washington, D.C. federal grand jury indicted both brothers on conspiracy to distribute cocaine and methamphetamine plus firearms charges (40-year mandatory minimum, up to two consecutive life sentences), stemming from a DEA-Los Angeles investigation spanning 2004–Dec 2023. El R-2 remains at large and is now a named U.S. target.
